scope: Research-only record of national ministry-reported crop activity, horticultural production, regional irrigation and wholesale price evidence, current seasonal risk and development programme indicators. Not a farm-profit calculator profile and not authorization to activate Eritrea.

currency.name: Eritrean nakfa
currency.note: The horticulture study reports Asmara wholesale prices in ERN per kilogram. No verified current farm-gate prices or farm input quotations are included.

context.agroecology: Semi-arid to arid highlands and lowlands with strong spatial differences in rainfall and irrigation access. Main-season rainfed cereal production is concentrated in central and western Anseba, Debub, Maekel and Gash Barka; Gash Barka is identified by FAO as the main crop-producing region. Irrigated horticulture is important in selected areas.
context.caution: Rainfed cereal performance is highly exposed to seasonal rainfall variability. Horticulture production and price observations in the research paper cover two sub-zobas and the Asmara wholesale market; they are not national averages or farm-gate quotations.

evidence.source: FAO Global Information and Early Warning System (GIEWS), Eritrea Country Brief
observations_text: Planting of the 2026 main-season crops was completed in July in central and western Anseba, Debub, Maekel and Gash Barka.

FAO reports poor Kiremti rainy-season performance associated with the ongoing El Niño event and says remote-sensing vegetation indicators show significant effects in several cropping areas, including Gash Barka.
FAO expects significant crop production shortfalls; this is a forecast/risk assessment, not a final 2026 harvest result.
evidence.caveat: Do not enter forecast shortfalls as measured production losses. Update after harvest and official post-harvest reporting.

observations.source_note: The ministry report attributes the increase to satisfactory summer showers and coordinated farmer/extension efforts; no national cereal tonnage is given in this summary.
Ministry-reported total; area reported as 4,800 ha.
Ministry-reported total; area reported as 14,000 ha.
Approximate number in the honey subsector, not honey output.
More than one million animals; vaccination programme coverage, not national herd size.

observations.indicator: Land treated with soil and water conservation measures
observations.source_note: Combined on-farm and off-farm area across six regions.

observations_text: Cereal crops listed include sorghum, pearl millet, teff, wheat, finger millet, barley and maize.
The ministry describes milk and egg production as subsectors requiring further improvement.
The ministry reports that 24 micro-dams were constructed during 2024 and around 22 were under construction at the time of reporting.
evidence.caveat: These are ministry-reported administrative/annual-assessment figures reproduced by the Ministry of Information, not a published census microdata table. The 138 percent figure is a reported year-on-year change, but the summary does not provide the underlying cereal tonnage or detailed crop-by-crop area/yield breakdown. Verify the full Ministry of Agriculture statistical tables before using them as model inputs.

evidence.topic: Small and Productive Farm Plot programme
evidence.source: Eritrea Ministry of Agriculture report published by the Ministry of Information, Ministry of Agriculture: 2024-Major Achievements

observations.source_note: More than 12,000 households across four summer-rainfall regions.
The ministry says some farmers harvested around 10 quintals, mainly wheat, from their small plot.

observations_text: The programme integrates cereals, pulses, oilseeds and vegetables, including sweet potato, using row planting, compost, improved seed and supplementary water where needed.
evidence.caveat: The 10-quintal figure is an example of some participating farmers, not a measured programme average or guaranteed yield. The programme plot size is a design parameter, not a national average farm size.

evidence.topic: Regional irrigated horticulture, production and wholesale price evidence
evidence.reference_period: Production and irrigated-area study 2015-2024; wholesale price index 2015-2025
evidence.source: Haile, Ramoelo, Dougill et al., Land Use/Land Cover (LULC) Change and Irrigated Area Monitoring in Eritrea: Insights into Horticultural Production and Sustainability, Remote Sensing in Earth Systems Sciences

observations.indicator: Irrigated area change in Gala Nefhi

observations.source_note: Total vegetables and fruits reported by study from Ministry of Agriculture data; output peaked at 48,174.5 tonnes in 2016 and 46,814.5 tonnes in 2019.
Study reports output rising from 4,282.8 tonnes in 2015; text highlights particularly strong vegetable growth.

observations.indicator: Rainfall coefficient of variation, Gala Nefhi

observations_text: The study's five-crop horticultural price index covers tomato, onion, potato, cabbage and banana.

Mean annual prices in Eritrean nakfa per kilogram were sourced from the Ministry of Agriculture Strategic Information Division using Asmara wholesale-market records; the index is a simple unweighted average with 2015=100.
The price index declined after 2015, reached its lowest point between 2019 and 2021, then recovered modestly.
The study reports that irrigated area expansion did not translate consistently into higher output in Dighe, while Gala Nefhi showed more synchronized irrigation and horticultural production growth.
The study's rainfall-production correlations were weak and statistically non-significant in both Dighe and Gala Nefhi.
evidence.caveat: The production series covers only Dighe and Gala Nefhi and combines fruit and vegetable output; it is not national crop-specific yield data. The Asmara observations are wholesale-market prices, not farm-gate prices. The accessible article text provides the index trend and methodology but not a complete machine-readable annual crop-by-crop price table. Satellite-derived irrigated-area change is a remote-sensing estimate, not a farm census.

evidence.topic: 2025 agricultural programme outcomes and extension support
evidence.source: United Nations Eritrea, Annual Results Report 2025

observations.indicator: Farmers supported with improved productivity and reduced losses
observations.source_note: More than 11,000 farmers; UN-supported programme result, not a national farmer census.

observations.indicator: Households benefiting from improved agricultural practices
observations.source_note: Report presents farmers and households as separate programme reach indicators.

observations.indicator: Coastal households adopting seaweed and sea-cucumber aquaculture
Coastal households reporting improved market/processing/storage access

observations_text: The UN report attributes farmer productivity and loss reductions to certified planting materials, improved pest control and agronomic techniques.

The report describes two years of value-chain analysis for banana, potato and anchovy, followed by investor engagement and investment interest in potato seed improvement, irrigation and anchovy value-chain development.
The report states that Eritrea's agricultural research institute and national plant and animal health laboratory now operate on solar power.
evidence.caveat: These are programme-reported reach and outcome indicators, not a national agricultural survey or independent causal impact evaluation. Do not treat expressions of investment interest as committed finance or completed investment.

observations_text: FAO reported favourable prospects for the 2025 main-season crops after early July rainfall deficits were offset by improved rainfall in August and an expectation of above-average rainfall for the remainder of the Kiremti season.
evidence.caveat: This is a seasonal outlook, not a final harvest result. It should not be compared directly with the September 2026 drought warning as though they were measured crop outcomes.

data_quality_and_use: The Ministry of Agriculture's 2024 report provides unusually useful national area and horticulture-output figures, but the accessible summary does not include crop-by-crop cereal tonnage, yield denominators or farm budgets.
The 2024 cereal harvest increase of 138 percent is a ministry-reported annual change; the baseline and absolute production volume need the underlying statistical tables.

The 2025 peer-reviewed remote-sensing study adds regional horticulture production trends and a documented wholesale price-index methodology for five crops, but its geographic scope is only Dighe and Gala Nefhi.

Asmara wholesale-market prices in ERN/kg are not producer prices. They must not be inserted as farm-gate revenue without verified farm-to-wholesale margins, grading, transport and marketing deductions.
FAO's September 2026 rainfall assessment indicates significant current-season production risk, particularly in Gash Barka and other main-season cropping regions.
UN programme reach figures are not national farmer counts or a representative farm survey.
No full crop-specific enterprise budgets, input cost schedules, labour costs or current producer price series have been verified.
missing_data_before_calculator_use: Obtain the Ministry of Agriculture's full 2024 statistical/annual assessment tables with crop-specific harvested area, production, yield, region, season and data collection method.
Obtain the 2025/2026 crop season final production and area results, including an assessment of the September 2026 rainfall deficit and harvest losses.

Extract the full Ministry of Agriculture Strategic Information Division annual Asmara wholesale price observations for tomato, onion, potato, cabbage and banana, with units, grades, dates and any missing-value notes.
Obtain comparable farm-gate prices by producing region and season, with farm-to-wholesale transport, handling, commissions, grading and loss deductions.
Obtain input prices for certified seed, planting material, fertilizer, compost, crop protection, labour, land preparation, irrigation equipment, pumping energy, water, packaging and transport.
Obtain representative crop enterprise budgets and crop calendars by region and irrigated/rainfed system, including marketable yield, crop cycles, labour and post-harvest losses.
Validate the Ministry's 2024 cereal, oilseed, pulse, fruit and vegetable statistics against National Statistics Office publications and FAOSTAT country rows.
Obtain livestock population, milk, egg, honey and meat production series and current animal/feed/veterinary prices before adding livestock enterprises.
Obtain project monitoring data and sampling methodology for farmer support programmes before using reported productivity gains as representative yield or income changes.
recommendation: Retain Eritrea as research-only. The evidence base is stronger than a simple international-database profile: it includes Ministry-reported 2024 national production and area figures, a peer-reviewed 2015-2024 regional horticulture/irrigation study with Asmara wholesale price methodology, UN programme outcomes and a current FAO September 2026 drought warning. However, no crop-level national yield series, current farm-gate prices or full enterprise budgets are yet verified. Do not activate Eritrea or calculate expected farm profit until the underlying Ministry tables, crop-specific price series and farm input budgets are extracted and reconciled.

administrative_geography.source: Proclamation No. 86/1996 for the Establishment of Regional Administrations, reproduced in FAOLEX; corroborated by Netherlands government country-of-origin report and WHO Eritrea country cooperation document.
administrative_geography.note: Eritrea's first-level administrative units are six zobas (regions). The cited legal source also describes lower sub-zoba and village/area administration levels; do not mix these lower units into the first-level selector.

audit_update: Batch 22 audit: verified six zoba regions and added them to the calculator region lookup. The matrix now distinguishes historical national area/output and combined regional horticulture evidence from crop-specific yield, wholesale from farmgate prices, and seasonal forecasts from final harvest data. Eritrea remains research-only; no active calculator profile or formula was changed.

notes: Selina Wamucii's October/September/November 2026 country price pages provide estimated retail and wholesale ranges around Asmara and Mitsiwa for selected commodities. They are market-level estimates, not verified producer/farmgate quotations, and do not identify producing region, grade, season or transaction date beyond the page's month label.
Do not map these figures into recommended farmgate price fields. Retain only as plausibility checks pending official market series or direct producer quotations.

currency_exchange_note_2026_11_03.caveat: The official peg is not proof of accessible foreign exchange or a market-clearing conversion rate. Preserve ERN as the calculator's domestic currency; do not use this peg to imply that wholesale USD estimates can be converted into actual farmgate quotations.
